title: fix(app): a saved machine file keeps its key order
body:
**Stacked on #478** (#383, the Machines pane edits and saves `.mch` files). The #480 work is a95093c0.

## What changed
A `.mch` saved from the Machines pane keeps the key order it was read in. Keys the file didn't have go at the end of their object. Project files are untouched.

- **New `crates/app/src/machine/order.rs`** (with provenance).
  - It reads the source text once and records the key order of every object and array as a `KeyOrder` tree. A duplicated key keeps its first position and takes its last value, like `serde_json::Value`.
  - `to_pretty(value, order)` writes the same layout as `to_string_pretty` (2-space indent, `": "`), with keys in the recorded order, then any unknown keys sorted.
- **`MachineDraft`** gains `order: KeyOrder`. `open` and `from_template` fill it from the source, `blank` leaves it empty, and `text()` writes through `to_pretty`. Edits still act on the plain `serde_json::Value`, so `fields.rs` is unchanged.
- **No new dependency, and `serde_json/preserve_order` is not turned on workspace-wide.** That would change every JSON writer, project files included. `indexmap` is already in the lock file, but using it directly would still be a dependency change, and the order visitor is about 60 lines.
- The `docs/decisions/383-machines-edit.md` "key order" entry is replaced by this decision.

## How tested
- `machine_edit::a_saved_file_keeps_its_key_order_and_new_keys_go_last`: a hand-written file in deliberately unsorted order, with unknown keys, gets an edit plus a new `spindle`/`max_speed` block. The saved file's exact key list is checked.
- `machine_edit::a_new_machine_writes_the_same_text_serde_json_would`: with no recorded order, the output matches `to_string_pretty` byte for byte.
- `machine_edit`, `machine_library`, `machine` and `project_roundtrip` (69) pass. Project files are byte-identical; no project writer changed.
- `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Limitation
Only the key order is kept. A hand-written file's inline arrays (e.g. `[0, 0, 1]` on one line) still come out multi-line.

Changelog: A machine file saved from the Machines pane keeps its key order (new keys go last) (#480)

Fixes #480

title: fix(machine): built-in lathe and mill-turn Z stroke in program coordinates
body:
## What changed

The built-in **Lathe** (`assets/machines/lathe.mch`) and **Mill-turn** (`assets/machines/millturn.mch`) stated a machine-frame Z stroke (`-615..0`, `-620..0`). The limit checker (`app::machine::check_document`) reads travel bands in **program coordinates through the work offset** (#457). With Z0 on the face, every move in front of it was out of stroke: clearance, approach, and facing allowance. No turning program posted on either built-in.

**Reproduced on main before the fix:** a face-and-turn job (Z0 on the finished face, 1 mm facing allowance, clearance Z 5) was refused on both machines, down to the facing approach (`Face1: move 0 reaches 0.800 in Z, the stroke is -615.000..0.000`).

Fix: Z is restated as the full stroke each way, the convention PR #477 applies to the VMC and tilt-head. Lathe Z is now `-615..615` and Mill-turn Z is `-620..620`. **X stays one-sided** (`0..320`, `0..650`). A lathe X is measured from the spindle centreline, and the centreline is the program's X0, so `0..R` is already a program-frame band. The Mill-turn Y (`-100..100`) was already symmetric. No checker code changed. This branch is off main, not stacked on #477. It leaves `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` and the module doc alone so the two PRs do not conflict; the convention text is in #477. The decision is in `docs/decisions/493-lathe-z-stroke.md`.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/lathe_stroke.rs`:
  - `a_turning_job_on_the_built_in_lathe_clears_the_face_and_posts` and `a_turning_job_on_the_built_in_millturn_clears_the_face_and_posts`: Facing plus Profile Rough on a flanged bar, clearance Z 5. `check_document` is clean, `verification_report` has no problems, and `post_setup` posts. Both failed on main.
  - `a_clearance_past_the_lathe_carriage_still_refuses_by_name` and `a_clearance_past_the_millturn_quill_still_refuses_by_name`: a clearance of L + 20 is refused with `Rough1: move N reaches 635.000 in Z, the stroke is -615.000..615.000` (and the 620 equivalent). There is no X complaint, and the post is refused.
  - `lathe_x_stays_a_centreline_band`: X stays `0..R` on both machines.
- These app suites all passed (debug): lathe_stroke, lathe_post, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_field_sim, lathe_field_tools, lathe_spindle_fit, lathe_spindle_keyed, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_cross_drill, turning, turning_profile, turning_bore, turning_holder, turning_blade, turning_contour, turning_contour_stock, turning_form, turning_thread, turning_axial_rapids, turning_stock_approach, turning_insert_zone, drill_prior, drill_prior_kinds, drilling_axial, c_axis_live, coolant_followups, carried_fixtures_cache, conformance, machine, machine_library, posting, setup_mount.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Posted G-code is unchanged: no golden NC/CL file changed, and the post scripts read no linear travel.

## Not exercised

- I did not run the ui crate suites. The ui crate is untouched. Its tests mount the built-in Lathe by name for door and route checks, but none of them reads the stroke.
- GUI and the headless MCP path were not run.
- The Mill-turn X `0..650` also judges its milling ops (live tooling). A milled feature in -X would still read as out of stroke. That is a separate question and is noted in the decision file.

Changelog: The built-in Lathe and Mill-turn machines state their Z stroke in program coordinates (full stroke each way), so turning programs with clearance in front of the face post instead of being refused.

title: feat(app): fixture library - save, insert and delete user fixtures
body:
**Stacked on #482** (#339 slice 4, fixture UX), which is on #476. Slice 6 of #339 per the triage on the issue: a fixture library.

## What changed
**The library file.** One `fixtures.camfixtures` in the user fixtures folder: `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES` (an absolute path), otherwise `<data dir>/camcraft/fixtures`, beside the machines folder.
- Versioned envelope: `{format: "camcraft-fixtures", version: 1, units: "mm", fixtures: [{name, note?, datum: {origin, rot}, facets}]}`. Save → load → save is byte-stable.
- **Refused by name, whole file:** bad JSON; wrong format, version or units; a missing name, datum or facets; a duplicate name; an empty mesh; a malformed facet; a rotation that isn't one; over 2M facets; the reserved `Machine/Table` name.
- A missing file reads as an empty library. A corrupt one is reported in the dialog, never shown as empty, and never overwritten.
- The atomic write mirrors #383's machine store. It's a short copy, to be folded into one helper once both land; see the decisions file.

**The datum.**
- An entry's facets are the fixture's own model-frame mesh, and its datum is a frame in that mesh.
- On insert, the model's pose is `P ∘ D⁻¹`, so the datum lands on the pick.
- The default datum is the model origin, so a fixture saved and re-inserted at its old pose stands exactly where it was. The other choice is "Bottom centre".

**Duplicate names:**
- In the library, saving an existing name asks "Replace …?". There is no silent rename.
- In the document, an inserted name that's taken lands as "Vise (2)", "Vise (3)" and so on.

**`InsertFixture`, one undo unit.** It spawns the model with the entry's facets, sets its pose, and tags it to the Fixtures node's setup. It refuses by name a setup that no longer exists, a non-finite or non-rotation pick, or a bad entry. There is no new project key: inserted fixtures are ordinary tagged models.

**Save and delete edit the library file.** They are save actions with confirmation, not undo entries, like machine files (#383).

**UI.** The setup's Fixtures node menu gains **Save fixture to library…** and **Insert from library…**, each a modal dialog.
- **Save:** the setup's fixtures as checkboxes, the datum choice, and a note.
- **Insert:** the entry list, X/Y/Z in display units, and roll/pitch/yaw. Buttons are Insert, **Delete from library…** (with confirmation) and Close.
- Picking the datum in the viewport is a follow-up.

All assets are user-made; no vendor libraries.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-library.md`

## How tested
- App `fixture_library` (6 tests):
  - envelope round-trip, and refusals by name;
  - the folder resolver;
  - save, replace and delete file edits;
  - the datum placement maths;
  - insert with undo, redo and the project round-trip.
- UI `egui_app::fixture_library_tests` (4 tests, driven through the real dialog):
  - the menu rows;
  - save, then the replace confirmation;
  - Insert queues one undoable command, and delete happens only after confirmation;
  - a corrupt library is named in the dialog.
- Regressions green: app `fixture_ux` 8, `fixtures` 14, `commands_undo` 32, `fixture_mesh` 3; ui lib 352, ui `tests/fixtures` 7, `tests/models` 4. One #482 test's menu-label list now includes the two new rows.

A hands-on check. The test kit is prepared and sandboxed with `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES`.

title: test(sim): pin that the fixture box laws already convict every mesh penetration
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 2 of #339, answered by tests rather than new law. The full analysis is posted on #339.

## What this is
Slice 2 asked whether the mesh law must also **convict**: catch penetrations the box laws let through.

**Answer: no.**
- A meshed fixture's box is the exact AABB of the same transformed vertices the mesh law reads (`model::entity_world_aabb` / `world_facets`). `mesh_refined` only reads a mesh whose AABB equals the law's box, and non-finite meshes keep the box verdict. So the mesh always sits inside its box, rotated fixtures and overhangs included.
- Every deliberate silence of the box laws allows an overlap of at most `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (1e-9) with the box. That covers the strict z overlap in `band_hits_box` (c2, plus #464's d2 upper bands and flute column) and the strict-dip rule in `rapid_hits_box`. An overlap that small with the box can't be more than that with the mesh.
- Everything else is an enclosure, not a silence.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs` (5 tests, with a gate-map header). Each composes the box laws with `mesh_refined` the way `posting::fixture_problems` does.
- **A mesh top face keeps the strict dip:** a retract off it, a traverse riding it and a cut riding it are silent. The same moves 0.001 lower report Rapid and Flute.
- **A rotated fixture's top edge is its box's top:** a block turned 45° about X, then 30° about Z.
- **An overhanging arm convicts the stack under it:** the Shank under the arm and the Holder rim off its end both hit. Its top stays flush-silent.
- **The #424 and #425 repros convict on a closed mesh** (Holder), from the box law and the mesh alike.
- **No straight move the box laws clear penetrates the mesh:** a seeded sweep of 12,000 moves biased onto flush planes. 7,045 are silent (103 in flush contact), and none penetrates the mesh. Lowering the box top 0.01 mm makes this test fail at once, which shows it catches real gaps.

## Found along the way (filed separately)
**#491:** the box laws judge an XY arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) is missed. This applies to every fixture, not only meshed ones, so the fix belongs in the box law. It is out of this slice's scope.

## How tested
- `fixture_mesh_convict` 5/5, `fixture_mesh` 9 passed (1 ignored), `fixture_stack_span` 8/8.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- Test-only: no product code changes.

Changelog: none (test-only)

title: feat(app): raise fixture-striking links and retracts over the steel
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 5 of #339 per the triage on the issue: link and retract routing around fixtures.

## What changed
New `crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs`, with one hook in `generate.rs` before the verify pass. It runs for upright mill paths only.

**The rule:**
- **What a link is:** the longest run of straight rapids between two non-rapid moves, or a path end.
- **When it counts as struck:** the gate's own fixture laws flag it. That's #464's whole-stack law (d2) plus #476's mesh acquittal, so a routed link is judged exactly as the post gate will judge it.
- **The fix:** a struck link becomes three G0 moves: up at its start XY, across, down to its end. The height is the higher of the link's own top and the highest box top under the traverse plus 5 mm (`ROUTE_GAP`). "Under the traverse" means every box the widest band reaches along the XY segment.
- **The cap:** the machine's stated Z stroke (WCS origin Z plus the top of the stroke), keeping at least 0.5 mm over the steel. Steel taller than that **refuses generation by name**: "the link at moves i..j … cannot clear fixture 'Clamp1': its steel stands to Z …, and the machine's Z stroke tops out at Z …". With no stroke stated there is no cap, as everywhere else.
- **Re-judging:** the re-laid link is judged again. If it's still struck, the steel stands over the link's own end column and no height helps. The link is then left as laid, its `FixtureHit` still blocks the post by name, and a path note says why.
- **Notes:** every raised link gets a path note: how many rose, from where, over which fixture, to what Z.

**Left as today (report-only):**
- **Keep-down feed links.** In the CL stream they look exactly like cuts, so lifting one could silently skip a cut. They're only taken inside the cut area, so if one hits steel the cuts beside it hit too, and the post is refused anyway. A keep-down **rapid** run at depth does become retract, traverse and plunge.
- **Other paths:** posed and rotary paths, lathe tools, paths with canned cycles (a traverse inserted between holes could post as a drill), thread or probe records, and runs inside a compensated span.

**Posted G-code changes only** for documents with a link the fixture laws strike, and only those links' G0 moves. Documents without fixtures return early untouched, and links that already clear are never rewritten, so all goldens are unchanged.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-routing.md`

## How tested
- **New app `fixture_route`** (6 tests):
  - A Contour around two blocks with a strap clamp to Z 40 between them, at clearance 25. As generated, the gate refuses ("strikes a fixture"). After the fix, the links rise to Z 45, the post is clean, the cuts are identical, and the note names Clamp1.
  - A clamp the links already clear leaves the path byte for byte.
  - A 100 mm Z stroke still routes over the 40 mm clamp, while a 400 mm clamp refuses generation naming 'Clamp1' and "Z 400.000".
  - A stay-down rapid link becomes retract, traverse and plunge. Clear steel and no steel are untouched.
  - Steel over a link's own end is left as laid and said.
  - A ceiling under the steel refuses, and a ceiling over it caps the rise.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** fixtures (14), fixture_mesh (3), fixture_law_gaps (3), posting (17), tool_body (8). All app test binaries passed in the quick gate.
- `clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
This changes posted G-code (raised G0 links) for documents with struck fixtures, so it's a draft until a Hub or machine run. It needs a project with a clamp between features.

Changelog: Links and retracts that would strike a fixture are raised over the steel (a clamp taller than the machine's Z stroke refuses generation by name) instead of only being reported (#339)

title: feat(sim): judge posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves against the fixture mesh
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 3 of #339 per the triage on the issue: posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves read against the fixture mesh. Slice 1 left those on the box verdict. As before, **the mesh only ever clears a hit the box law flagged; it never adds one.**

## What changed
**Frames.**
- **Path frame:** steel that turns with the part, and any steel when no rotary axis is stated (the box laws' frame).
- **Machine frame, A rotary:** fixed steel under an A rotary op, carried per stretch by `posed_steel::upright_turn`, the same frame `workholding` uses. A pose the rotary alone can't stand upright keeps the box verdict.
- **Machine frame, spindle C:** each move's C line is recovered from its two stated C angles. Fixed steel gets one exact sweep of the machine's straight station run. Steel turning with the part is read along the real spiral, in stretches turned by −C.
- **XZ/YZ arcs:** chorded in their own plane, with the same sagitta pad as XY arcs.
- **Left to the box:**
  - a C move whose start C isn't the previous move's;
  - a non-horizontal C pose;
  - a C turn under 1e-4 rad or near 180°;
  - a held C under fixed steel;
  - fixed steel under both a rotary axis and C;
  - an arc on a C move.

**Why a "clear" is safe.**
1. Each posed move is split into stretches by its pose turn (`midpose::turn_intervals`). Over a stretch the tip stays on its segment within the chord pad, and the pose stays within `swing` of the stretch axis, by midpose's existing rate bound.
2. A band point `p(t) + Q(t)y` stays within `swing·hypot(max(|lo|,|hi|), r)` of the unturned band. So the band lies inside segment ⊕ oriented cylinder ⊕ ball(pad), a convex set.
3. GJK sweeps the segment and cylinder exactly, and the ball goes into the margin. "Clear" is returned only with a separating-plane proof. A non-finite input or NaN margin counts as a hit.
4. A turn into another frame adds `dth·ρmax`, with ρmax taken at the stretch's four parallelogram corners plus r + pad. Distance to a line is convex, so that bounds it.
5. Consecutive stretches overlap at their shared instant, so one inside-the-solid point per band decides. Using an oriented cylinder rather than a capsule means a tilted tool isn't falsely convicted on a vise floor below its tip.

**Labels.** A mesh-kept rapid hit names a band above the flute by its part (Shank, Holder, Spindle), like #464's law (d2). This now applies on the posed and C paths too.

`docs/decisions/339-mesh-posed.md`, including a finding filed as **#486**: `cl::stamp_c` pieces keep the whole move's tool axis, so the box laws may misjudge fixed steel on C turns. The mesh can't fix that, since it only clears hits.

## How tested
- **New sim `fixture_mesh_posed`** (9 tests, plus 1 heavy-lane):
  - a tilted pass, an in-place index and a tilted rapid down a vise gap are cleared, while the same index into a jaw and a rapid swung into the other jaw still convict;
  - A-rotary fixed and turning steel, each with a clear case and a convicting case;
  - C turns with turning and fixed steel; a move with no prior C, and an axial tool, keep the box verdict;
  - XZ arcs, one clear and one dipping 0.21 mm into the base; a YZ arc in the gap is clear;
  - a posed rapid kept by the mesh names its band;
  - both turn signs (A and C) pinned by mutation.
- **New app `fixture_mesh_posed`** (2 tests): a 3+2 face indexed B 10° between closed jaws. The box law alone convicts every move, yet the post and generation are clean. With the jaws 1 mm into reach, the post is blocked and generation warns.
- **One slice-1 pin renamed** (`unpaired_boxes_keep_the_box_verdict_and_posed_moves_are_read`): a posed gap pass is now cleared.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** posed_fixture, posed_fixture_midpose, posed_rapids, midmove_pose, fixture_stack_span, sim lib; app fixtures, rotary_fixtures, fixture_mesh, fixture_law_gaps. Their fixtures are box-only or open, so the mesh never judges them.
- **Performance:**
  - debug, 29.7k facets and 80 posed moves: 0.07 s;
  - release heavy lane, 203k facets and 2000 posed moves: 0.33 s.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
No GUI or G-code change. More 4/5-axis and rotary programs now post: those whose only "hit" was a box around empty space between jaws.

Changelog: Fixture collisions on tilted, rotary and spindle-C moves and XZ/YZ arcs are judged against the fixture's real mesh too, so a tilted pass between vise jaws no longer refuses the post (#339)

title: fix(sim): sweep XY arcs on the true circle in the field engine and envelope scan
body:
## What changed
This is the follow-up to #402 / PR #414. Two more places drew XY arcs (G2/G3 in G17) as chords inside the arc: the **field engine** (`field_cut::chords`) and the **envelope scan** that runs while toolpaths are generated (`stock_sim/scan.rs`). Both now read the true circle.

**Field engine:** new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_arc.rs`, 284 lines, with a provenance header.
- An upright mill tool's XY arc is now cut as `Sweep::Arc` pieces.
- Pieces follow the old chord budget, capped at a quarter turn. So the lattice windows and the `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` limit refuse exactly what they refused before. Each window grows by its piece's sagitta.
- **Level piece:** solved exactly in closed form. The nearest tool pose is at the point's own bearing, clamped to the piece. It uses the column engine's tie rules (`flat_tie`, `bull_tie`), and `field_ray` gets the exact floor plane from it.
- **Helical piece:** searched with `dexel_arc::piece_min`, #414's search (samples, then a golden section). Every result is a real distance evaluation plus the usual 1e-12 margin, so the field never shows material removed that the tool did not cut. Its `residual` is a proven bound: half a sample step of tool travel.
- Tilted tools, lathe tools and XZ/YZ arcs keep their chords.

**Envelope scan:** new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_arc.rs`, 146 lines.
- Each arc piece keeps the chord `arc_chords` drew. That chord is now only used for indexing (bins, boxes, ring ids, the ridge law's pass counting), so all of that is unchanged.
- Every distance the verdict uses is now measured to the arc:
  - point distances for rest, flank and hidden rest (exact for level arcs);
  - facet distances for gouge, searched only when the chord is within the piece's bulge of the ball.
- The gouge bin walk, the ridge boxes and the `SegGrid` ring prune each grow by the bulge (`sag + |dz|`), so no contact the chords caught can be missed.

**Tests tightened:** `stock_bull_nose::both_engines_cut_a_bull_nose_alike` now holds the helix arc to the same 1e-5 engine parity as straight moves, and the `arc_parity` relaxation is removed.

The decisions and the dropped alternatives (straddling chords, finer chords, one whole-arc sweep) are in `docs/decisions/413-arc-chords-field.md`.

## Pinning tests

title: fix(sim): judge a gouge with tol of lateral slack at a wall
body:
## What changed

The program sim's gouge verdict judged each column by height alone, at its centre. A height verdict's normal-distance tolerance is `tol * cos(slope)`, which is zero at a vertical wall. So a column whose centre sits a few microns inside a wall, reached by a tool that finishes that wall within tolerance, was charged the wall's whole height, and the post gate refused a correct program.

- New `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/wall_slack.rs`: a gouge candidate (a column more than `tol` below the part's top at its centre) is re-judged against the lowest part top within `tol` of its centre. That is the centre plus an eight-direction ring at radius `tol`, and air counts as lowest. If the column is within `tol` of that lowest top, it is clean. Otherwise it is a gouge, charged at the centre's own depth as before.
- Both engines use it: the column engine (`deviate`) and the field arm (`deviate_field`), keeping the stage-C parity law.
- Rest is unchanged: it is still judged against the centre's own top.
- The extra cost is paid only when gouge candidates exist. A clean program costs nothing extra.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/299-wall-column-gouge.md`. It covers why the slack is `tol` and not the issue's `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, cell)`, and the other options that were dropped.

## Readings (current main 5fd2b93)

- The issue's exact 2D Contour repro (model stock, 10 mm deep) **no longer reproduces on main**: the gate is clean before and after this change. It is kept as a regression test.
- 3D Finish, `BN-0600`, kind defaults, model stock (the issue's MCP job): before, `gouge: ... 1 cell(s), worst 10.21 mm at (16.69, -24.91, z 9.79)`. Probing that column, its centre is 1-3 um inside the D's wall, with air beyond. After: no gouge. The post is still blocked, by the generator's own `ShankHit` warnings, which is a separate matter.
- 3D Finish in the issue's 70 x 70 x 27 box at z -7: before, 37 cells, worst 22.01 mm at (-26.56, 13.94). After: 0 gouge cells.

## Tests

- `crates/sim/tests/wall_slack.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `a_column_a_few_microns_inside_a_finished_wall_is_not_a_gouge`: both engines, with a floor beside the wall and with air beside it. This test fails on main.
  - `the_old_law_charged_that_column_the_whole_wall`
  - `a_real_gouge_into_a_wall_still_convicts_at_its_full_depth`: covers 50 um, 12 um and 1 mm intrusions, in both engines, and checks the full 15 mm depth and location.
  - `a_floor_gouge_away_from_walls_is_unchanged`
  - `rest_beside_a_wall_keeps_the_centres_own_top`
- `crates/app/tests/wall_column_gouge.rs` (new, 3 tests):
  - `a_3d_finish_on_the_users_part_reads_no_gouge_at_its_wall`: fails on main.
  - `a_3d_finish_in_the_users_box_stock_reads_no_gouge_at_its_wall`: fails on main.
  - `the_issues_contour_on_model_stock_reads_no_gouge`
- Gate results:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: all green.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app` (all 169 binaries, debug): all green.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- Release `--ignored` lanes:
  - sim `hidden_rest_banded`, app `operations` and `rotary_field_parity`: green.
  - app `stock_engine_agreement` has 2 tests (`both_engines_judge_every_golden_program_alike`, `the_feed_sampler_reads_every_golden_program_alike`) that **fail identically on upstream/main** (6467 FINDING lines, for example `contour_disc_hole.cl` column (46.25, -4.25) and `finish3d_scallop_plateau.cl+bull` engagement). This is pre-existing and not caused by this PR. Diffing the findings between main and this branch shows 5 lines changed: field-arm micro-readings on `finish3d_project_dome.cl` (field dev -0.011 to -0.016 on the slope) now read clean instead of gouge. That is the expected slope allowance (at most `tol * tan(slope)`). No column-engine verdict changed, and no golden changed.

title: feat(sim): judge fixture collisions against the fixture's real mesh
body:
**Replaces #430**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so it can no longer be updated. This branch carries the merges with main through #461: the mesh law reads #381's `HolderStack` (`steel_stack(geom, holder, spindle)`, with `mesh_refined` wrapping the `*_held` laws), and #395's turning holder judge is kept. The recipe in the old 'merge note for #381' below is now done.

Slice 1 of #339 (triage and split are on the issue). Fixture collisions are judged against the fixture's real mesh, so a path down a vise's gap posts clean.

## What changed
**The box laws still run first, and the mesh can only clear a hit.** When a fixture's world box flags an upright move (laws c2 and d2), the fixture's closed mesh gets the final say, and it can only clear that hit, never add one. That keeps the box laws' deliberate silences, such as a retract off the mounting face. Where nothing is cleared, output is identical to before, labels included.

**Test shape.** Each tool band (flute, shank, holder, and the spindle housing when stated) is an upright cylinder swept along the move, an exact convex shape. Arcs are split into chords, each padded by how far the true arc can stray from it, plus 1 µm.

**Why it can't miss a real hit:**
- A band counts as clear only when a GJK distance test proves a gap of more than `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (plus the arc pad) to every nearby triangle. If the search fails or runs out, the answer is a hit.
- A band far from every triangle could still be buried inside the solid, so a point of it is tested by ray parity. Six fixed off-axis rays are tried; any that graze an edge, vertex or face are discarded, and if all are ambiguous the point counts as inside.
- Only closed meshes judge (each edge used once in each direction).
- A bounding-volume tree over the triangles is pruned with the same proof at every node.

**What keeps the box verdict:**
- Meshes that are open, non-finite, fully collapsed or over 4M facets: a named `MeshError`, logged.
- Tilted moves, moves with a non-zero C angle, and XZ/YZ arcs.
- Lathe tool kinds and non-mill machines.
- A box shared by two fixtures.

**Performance (release):**
- A 203k-facet closed mesh: validate and build the tree in 0.05 s.
- Worst case, 2000 passes grazing it 0.05 mm off (every one inside its box): 0.74 s total (0.37 ms/move), all correctly cleared.

**Code:**
- New: `crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/` (mod, gjk, bvh, ray), `crates/sim/src/verify/mesh_steel.rs`.
- Hooks: `fixture::meshes_for`, plus small edits in `operation/{job,generate}.rs` and `posting.rs` (meshes cached once per setup).
- `docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md`

**Merge note for #381:** this edits next to #381's `HolderStack` changes in `posting.rs` `fixture_problems` and `generate.rs` `workholding_warnings`. Whichever lands second resolves by keeping `mesh_refined(path, &wh, &steel, rapids, |w| <law>)` with the closures calling #381's `_held` variants, and by building `steel_stack` from the `HolderStack` bands. The decisions file has the recipe.

## How tested
- `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (8 tests, plus one in the heavy lane):
  - a vise-gap pass, plunge and arc are cleared;
  - a jaw-corner clip still hits, while the same line 4.95 mm off is cleared;
  - a jaw-face clip, a holder over a jaw, a rapid into a jaw top, and a tool buried in steel all still hit;
  - open, NaN, empty and collapsed meshes refuse by name and keep the box verdict;
  - a tilted move and a fixture-less table box keep the box verdict;
  - timings (heavy lane: the 200k-facet case).
- `crates/app/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (3 tests), end to end through `posting::verification_gate` and regeneration:
  - vise jaws 3 mm off the pass: clean;

title: feat(mcp): serve the MCP tool table live from inside the GUI
body:
> Replaces #428, moved to the new fork (the old one left NeoTech's network; a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in; the one conflict was the module list in `mcp/mod.rs`, where both sides are kept. `mcp` 9/9, `mcp_live` 6/6 and `mcp_pick` 2/2 pass, and clippy for app and ui is clean. Still a draft, waiting on the hands-on GUI check (refreshed binaries `camcraft-ui-428` and `camcraft-cli-428`).

## What changed
The GUI can host the same MCP tool table (`app::mcp`) live, so an agent drives the open document and the user watches it in the viewport.

- **Opt-in, loopback only.** Off by default; started with `--mcp-port <n>` / `--mcp-port=<n>` or `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT` (flag wins; `0` picks a free port). Binds 127.0.0.1. A bad value exits 2.
- **Transport:** plain TCP carrying the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC as `camcraft-cli mcp`, plus a stdio<->TCP bridge `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` so stdio MCP clients can attach.
- **Threading:** a std listener thread (one client at a time) only moves text; each line goes over an mpsc channel to the UI thread with its own reply channel and wakes the idle winit loop (`EventLoopProxy`). No world access off the UI thread.
- **Same document, same History.** The UI thread answers in `State::drain_actions` after the user's own queued commands, through the existing `Server` dispatch (no tool code duplicated): the `Env` gets the GUI's world handle and borrows the GUI's own `History` for the call. An agent step is one Ctrl+Z, and the agent's `undo`/`redo` walk the user's steps too. Every call bumps `doc_version`; the status line reads `agent: <tool>`.
- **Status strip** shows `MCP listening on 127.0.0.1:<port>` while the server runs (default frames unchanged).
- **Never crash:** malformed JSON -> -32700; a dropped client, closed channel or >16 MiB line is logged and the listener carries on; dropping the `Inbox` stops and joins the thread (~50 ms) at shutdown.
- **Refused live:** `open_project` (would replace the user's document past the unsaved-changes prompt).
- New code: `crates/app/src/mcp/{listen,live,bridge}.rs`, `crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs`; `mcp/tools.rs` and `mcp/edit.rs` untouched.

## Maintainer note (judgement call)
There is no authentication: any local process can drive the open document while the server is on. Being off by default and loopback-only is the guard; a token could be added later if wanted. `save_project` without a path saves over the open project but does not mark it clean, so the app may still ask to save. A long `generate` blocks the UI frame for its duration.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1722 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. Hand run: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7333` driven through `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` (set_stock, add_tool, add_operation all `isError:false`; `get_job` over nc showed the op in the app's world).

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/mcp_live.rs`: `a_live_call_lands_on_the_callers_history_and_its_undo_reverts_it`, `each_agent_step_is_one_undo_step_on_the_shared_history`, `the_live_session_refuses_open_project_and_reads_bad_lines_as_errors`, `the_port_flag_is_opt_in_and_checked`, `a_loopback_client_drives_the_owners_document_and_survives_bad_input` (real loopback TCP), `the_bridge_copies_stdio_to_a_live_session_and_back`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::mcp_live`: `an_agents_operation_shows_in_the_browser_and_ctrl_z_removes_it`, `the_status_strip_says_the_server_is_listening`.

## Not exercised
Ctrl+Z pressed by hand in the real window (harness only) - **draft until the GUI check**; Windows/Linux runs (std::net only); a real MCP client app beyond the bridge/nc; the bind-failure path (port in use). Posted G-code unchanged.

**Tool editor: a "Tool body" column.**

- The 2D profile preview draws the placed body's revolved envelope in amber over the cylinders.
- A tool not yet in the document shows "Add the tool first…".

**Picking.** A click casts a ray through `tool_body_view::pick`.
- **Pick tip** snaps to the nearest corner of the hit facet and sets the offset so that corner is the tip.
- **Pick axis** takes the clicked facet's outward normal.
- Picks only fill the fields; they never queue a command.

**Simulation.** While the transport runs, the running tool's body is posed at the playhead (read from the cached timeline) and drawn as a shaded, depth-tested part. A tool without a body draws exactly as before.

**App-layer helpers**, so ui stays thin: `crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs` holds `load`, `preview` (the same place-and-envelope step as the command, uncommitted), `pick`, `tip_offset_at`, `posed` and `body_for_operation`.

**A new program-entry kind: Pause (M0), Optional stop (M1) and Go home.**
- Entries sit in the operation list alongside operations, using the same `OperationMeta.order`.
- The new component `schema::ProgramEntry { action, setup, suppressed }` is not an `Operation`. - An entry has no generated status, so it never holds the post as "not generated".

**Posting.** Each entry folds into the posted op before it, as that op's `PARAM AfterOperation` word (one hook in `posting::op_streams`, logic in `program_entry::posted_afters`).
- A Pause after Face1 posts byte-identically to setting Face1's after-action to Program stop. This is pinned for all three actions on Fanuc and Haas.
- Equal asks in one gap merge, and a program stop absorbs an optional stop.
- An entry after a suppressed op attaches to the last op that posts.
- Suppress and "Skip pauses and homes" mute entries just as they mute op actions.
- **Refused by name:**
  - an entry before every posted op;
  - a Pause and a Home in the same gap (the stream holds one after-word per gap);
  - entries on the Tormach post, which doesn't read `AfterOperation`, the same as the per-op action there today.

- An entry row uses the Post glyph, with its action and SUPPRESSED in the suffix. Its menu offers change action, suppress, delete and add after.

- An entry saves as `"kind": "entry"` plus an `entry` payload.

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
**Stacked on #437** (#418), which is on #433 (#417) and #432 (#416). Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the #419 work is 68bd14a5. Part of #363.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

title: feat(post): probing on an inverted X/Y axis for the Fanuc post
body:
Part of #372. Lifts the #374 refusal of probing on an inverted X/Y, for Fanuc. Haas follows when its probing hooks land (PR #360), hence `Refs #392`.

## What changed
- **Translation.** `post::invert` mirrors the probing records on an inverted X/Y, the same way it mirrors a move. It negates the TOUCH target and expected trip, the RETREAT back-off delta and its end point, and each FOUND axis's expected value.
- **New manifest flag `probeAxisInversion = true`.** The translation runs only for a post script that declares it, and only `fanuc.cps` does. Haas declares `axisInversion` but not this flag, so it refuses probing by name. Posts without `axisInversion` already refuse any inverted machine.

**Why negating is right.** The controller position is `M = G54 + P`, and the tip stands at `S·M`, where S = −1 on the inverted axis.
- The posted `P = S(W − origin)` lands correctly only if G54 holds `S·D`.
- A part off by d trips at `S(W_trip + d − origin)`. The translated expected value is `S(W_trip − origin)`, so the deviation is `S·d`.
- `G10 L2 X[#5221+dev]` then gives `S(D + d)`: the real part's datum in controller coordinates.
- Back-offs are increments, so they flip with the axis. `ABS[dev]` and the choice of travel axis are sign-free.
- In full: `docs/decisions/392-probe-inverted-axis.md`.

## How tested
New `inverted_probe` (8 tests). The posted Fanuc programs run on a **test-only macro-B controller** (`crates/app/tests/macro_b/`): G31 trips where the stylus first meets a simulated part, every G0/G1 is collision-checked, and unmodelled words are errors.
- **Physical offset:** face −Z, face −X, edge −Y, corners +X+Y and −X−Y, bore and boss, each on standard, inverted-X, inverted-Y and inverted-XY machines, with the part shifted (0.37, −0.21, −0.13) mm.
  - G55 always ends at the physical datum, within 0.002.
  - G54 is untouched, and unmeasured axes aren't written.
  - The standard machine gives the same answer, which checks the interpreter.
- **Edge cases:** a part exactly on the model returns the datum unchanged. No contact raises `#3000=2`, and out of tolerance raises `#3000=1`.
- **Converse checks:** the untranslated program misses on an inverted machine. Undoing any one translated word breaks it: a stylus crash, a tolerance alarm, or probing past overtravel.
- **Both sign forms:** the reader accepts the old `#100--2.5` and the folded `#100+2.5` from #386, which is now on main. Re-run after merging main: 8/8.
- **Existing suites:** `inverted_post`, `inverted_equivalence`, `axis_direction`, `probe_op`, `probe_reach`, `fanuc_post`, `conformance` and the camcraft-post suites pass. **No golden changed.** `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except #415, which is red on main.

## Not exercised
No run on a real control with an inverted axis. The macro interpreter proves the arithmetic and motion of the posted words.

Changelog: Probing posts on a Fanuc machine with an inverted X/Y axis (the probe records are mirrored like moves; the written work offset is the physical correction) (#392)

title: fix(sim): fixture laws judge the whole tool stack over each move's true height span
body:
Two P0 gaps in the fixture box laws: silent crashes the post gate let through. Both were found surveying #339.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/src/verify/stack_span.rs` gives both laws one rule for the z span of the tool stack along a move.
- Each piece of the tip path (the straight move, or one of an arc's 3-D chords) spans `[min(floor, piece low), piece high]`.
- A band `above..above+len` is judged over `[z_lo+above, z_hi+above+len]` with the existing strict `band_hits_box`.
- That window only ever grows compared with the old one. On a level move it is the old window, with the same arithmetic.

**#425, law c2 (`bands_vs_fixtures_held`).** Every band, including the flute column and the leaning enclosure, is judged over its true span along the move, floored at the move's deepest end. Before, every band was pinned at `min(from.z, to.z)`.
- The repro: a ramp z0→40 under a clamp arm at z100..120 over its high end, holder top at 130 there. It now reports `FixtureHit(Holder)`.
- A non-finite z now counts as a hit. The old `min` dropped NaN silently.

**#424, law d2 (`rapids_vs_fixtures_held`, upright branch).** After the flute disc (unchanged, still reported as `Rapid`), the rapid now checks every band above the flute over the rapid's span, each named when struck: shank, **the `HolderStack`'s own bands**, and the spindle housing at `holder.top`. The flute column above the tip comes last.
- The vertical retract beside the r20-holder bolt reports Holder. A low traverse past a tall bolt reports Shank, or Spindle.
- **Strict-dip silences kept:** a retract off a mounting face, a plunge onto a face, a traverse riding a face, and flush contact all stay silent. Penetrating by 0.001 reports.

**With #381 (merged).** The upright-rapid stack is built from the same `HolderStack` the bands law and the posed sweep take, so a modelled holder body is judged band by band. `fixture_stack_span::an_upright_rapid_reads_a_modelled_holder_bodys_bands` pins it: a slim r5 cylinder clears the bolt, and the body's r20 collar must hit.

`docs/decisions/424-425-fixture-law-gaps.md`

## How tested
- **New sim `fixture_stack_span`** (8 tests):
  - the #424 retract, also through `rapids_vs_workholding` for turning, fixed and rotary steel;
  - the traverse naming Shank and Spindle;
  - an overhanging arm caught by the flute column;
  - the strict-dip pins;
  - the #425 ramp in both directions, and a helical ramp;
  - level moves unchanged;
  - the HolderStack test.

  6 of the 8 fail on main before this fix. The strict-dip and level-move pins pass on both, by design.
- **New app `fixture_law_gaps`** (3 tests): a face program whose retract, and whose plunge start, carry the holder into a clamp arm. `posting::verification_gate` refuses with "Face1: holder at move N strikes a fixture", and generation warns `FixtureHit`. The same arms at the holder's top post clean. The two blocking tests fail on main.
- **Existing suites, no verdict changed:** fixtures, rotary_fixtures, tool_body, posting, and the posed/rapids suites pass. The window is a superset of the old one, so old hits are never dropped; new hits come only from steel the stack really reaches. On long ramps the enclosing window can over-report a graze. That trade-off is chosen over an exact sheared sweep, which would drop some existing verdicts; see the decisions file.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean. `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except #415, which is red on main.

## Merging with #430 (fixture mesh)
A trial merge is clean. #430 wraps these laws and can only clear a hit. On a meshed fixture, an upright-rapid holder hit reads as `Rapid` rather than `Holder`. That's a label difference only; the post is blocked either way.

title: fix(ui): macOS Cmd+Q asks about unsaved changes
body:
> Replaces #334, which GitHub closed when its review fix was pushed after the fork left NeoTech's network. It includes that fix: `os_quit::request()` is `#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", test))]`, so it is not dead code on Windows or Linux under clippy. The hands-on Cmd+Q check on macOS passed (see #334).

## What changed

On macOS, Cmd+Q, the app menu's Quit, the Dock's Quit and a logout all send `terminate:` to NSApplication. winit 0.30.13's app delegate has no `applicationShouldTerminate:`, so AppKit ended the process at once. `CloseRequested` never arrived, and the unsaved-changes prompt (#107) was skipped. The menu also takes Cmd+Q before egui sees it, so the egui Cmd/Ctrl+Q shortcut never fired on macOS either.

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/os_quit.rs`. On macOS, `install()` adds `applicationShouldTerminate:` to winit's delegate class through `class_addMethod`. The method answers `NSTerminateCancel` and only sets an atomic flag, so nothing can unwind across the FFI boundary. `class_addMethod` never replaces a method: if a future winit adds its own handler, the hook logs that and stays out. A missing AppKit, app or delegate is logged, never a panic. On other platforms `install()` does nothing.
- `route_pending(state)` turns the flag into `actions::quit`, the same guarded Quit the window X sends. The shell calls it in `about_to_wait`, and un-minimises and focuses the window so the prompt is seen. A clean document quits through `el.exit()`, which does not go back through `terminate:`.
- Dependency: `objc2 0.5`, the same binding and version winit already pulls in. It is macOS-only (`[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]`), and no new crate enters `Cargo.lock`.

Decisions and the alternatives dropped are recorded in `docs/decisions/144-macos-cmd-q.md`: retargeting the menu item, replacing winit's default menu, and routing to `performClose:`.

Side effect: cancelling the terminate also cancels a logout or shutdown while CamCraft is open, and macOS says CamCraft stopped it. That is the usual document-app behaviour. Letting the logout continue after the user answers was left out.

## Readings

- winit 0.30.13: `platform_impl/macos/menu.rs` wires Quit to `terminate:`, and `app_state.rs` implements only `applicationDidFinishLaunching:` and `applicationWillTerminate:`.
- Live run on a Mac: a debug build with a clean document, sent `terminate:` via `NSRunningApplication.terminate`. The request went through the hook, and the app then exited with code 0.

## Pinning test

- `egui_app::tests::unsaved::os_quit_request_over_unsaved_changes_prompts_once`: an OS quit request over unsaved work is routed once, does not exit, and shows "Unsaved changes"; Don't Save then quits.

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` ran as batch (Cargo files touched). Green apart from the known swarf_pose_continuity and the GPU-adapter headless tests (headless_run_succeeds, egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero, headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero: no graphics adapter in this environment). clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Manual check (needs a Mac)

1. `cargo run -p camcraft-ui`, then make the document dirty (the title gets `*`).
2. Press Cmd+Q. The prompt should appear. Click Cancel: the app stays open.
3. Choose app menu > Quit. The prompt should appear. Click Don't Save: the app quits.
4. Make it dirty again and minimise. Right-click the Dock icon > Quit. The window should come back with the prompt.
5. With a clean document, Cmd+Q quits at once.

Changelog: macOS: Cmd+Q, the app menu's Quit and the Dock's Quit ask Save / Don't Save / Cancel over unsaved changes instead of quitting at once (#144)

title: fix(sim): refuse carrying stock between setups on different machines
body:
> Replaces #411, which GitHub closed when a review fix was pushed after the fork left NeoTech's network. This branch is #411's plus that fix.

**Review fix (from #411's review):** the machine check now runs only where material crosses: in `carry_turn` for a carry, and in `walk`'s Clip arm. A later setup that takes its own new block on another machine is judged, not refused. Pinned by `setup_carry::a_new_block_on_another_machine_is_judged_not_refused`; setup_carry passes 9/9 and clippy is clean.

## What changed
Follow-up from the review of #401 (carry the machined body into the next setup).

**The missing refusal.** #401's notes credit the cross-machine refusal to "#390's refusal", but no such check existed in the program sim. #390 is the browser tree. The only mount refusals (#343) sit at generation and at post, and the sim walk checked only the **active** setup's machine kind.

Changes in `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs` (the constant is re-exported from `stock_sim.rs`):
- **New refusal:** `CARRY_MACHINE_REFUSAL`, raised by `one_machine(world, from, to)`. It compares the two setups' own machines (`setup_mount::machine_of`: the setup's machine, else the document's). The message names both setups and both machines, e.g. `'Setup1' on no machine, 'Setup2' on Tormach 770M`.
- **At the carry:** `carry::entry` refuses a carry onto another machine. The lathe/mill-turn check now reads the two setups' shared machine instead of the active setup's. Because `entry` is shared with the rest reading (#318), an op in the later setup is refused at generation with `REST_CARRY_REFUSAL` plus the machine reason.
- **In the program walk:** `carry::walk` (behind `simulate_document` and `incoming_body`) refuses every setup change onto another machine. That includes a clip between setups that hold the part the same way, because a clip keeps what the earlier setup left standing.
- **Clip in the rest reading:** deliberately **not** refused. There, the later setup starts from its own block and reads nothing across. Refusing it would block generation in every two-machine document whose setups hold the part alike, which #343 allows.

**Off-grid alignment** is represented exactly, so it is pinned rather than refused. `Body::carry` takes the image origin from the turned lattice corners, so every image cell centre is a transformed source centre, and nothing snaps to the old grid.

`docs/decisions/317-carry-body.md` is left unedited, per the decisions README (a PR does not edit another PR's file). `docs/decisions/404-carry-machine-check.md` records the correction.

## Pinning tests
- `sim/tests/stock_carry.rs::an_odd_lattice_carried_off_the_grid_keeps_whole_cells`: a 7 × 5 lattice at 0.5 mm with a distinct height per column. It is carried through a flip over X and a quarter turn, each translated by (0.37, −1.13). The test checks a one-to-one column map, image centres equal to the transformed source centres, exact heights, and exact origin, volume and bounds.
- `app/tests/setup_carry.rs::a_carry_between_setups_on_different_machines_is_refused_by_name`: generation is refused naming both setups and both machines. `simulate_document` and `incoming_body` error, and undo restores the carry bit for bit.
- `app/tests/setup_carry.rs::a_clip_between_setups_on_different_machines_is_refused_by_name`: generation still works, and the program sim refuses by name.
- `app/tests/setup_carry.rs::a_flip_about_a_centre_off_the_grid_carries_whole_cells`: a part centred off-grid in a 61 × 47 block, flipped. The incoming body is the exact mirror, and the verdict shows no gouge.

## Readings
- These suites all pass: `setup_carry` 8, `rest_across_setups` 5, `stock_sim_document` 9, `setup_align` 9, `setup_mount` 6, `setup_relative` 8, `setups` 11, app lib 95, `stock_carry` 7, `stock_sim` 24.
- **Quick gate:** post, sim and app are green. The remaining reds also fail on main: `swarf_pose_continuity` (#351) and the GPU headless tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

title: Add orthographic (parallel) viewport projection
body:
Orthographic (parallel) viewport projection, issue #434.

**What changed**

- `Camera` grows a `projection: ProjectionMode` field; `Perspective` stays
  the default. The mode rides the camera itself, so `mvp`, `ray_through`
  and `dolly_cursor` share one decision by construction and every existing
  `mvp(aspect)` call site keeps working untouched. `frame`, `toward` and
  `oriented` carry it; orbit, pan and zoom leave it alone.
- Ortho branch: an affine matrix (clip.w is 1, linear depth), view
  half-height `dist * tan(30 deg)` - exactly the height perspective sees
  at the target plane - so the mode switch never jumps the framing and
  `dist` keeps spelling zoom for orbit, pan and frame alike. Pick rays go
  parallel through the same matrix, and the ortho dolly holds the world
  point under the cursor.
- Ephemeral view state, like the Solids radios: a direct field flip
  through `actions::toggle_projection`, never a command, never saved in
  the project; the sim's `PreviewCamera` stays perspective.
- UI: a Projection radio row (Perspective / Ortho) under the Solids radios
  in the browser pane, and bare P in `shortcuts()` toggles it with the
  same guard as bare F, so Ctrl+P keeps its post dialog and the Alt lanes
  stay clear.

**Pinned by**

`projection_tests` in `crates/ui/src/law_tests.rs`: the ortho matrix is
affine where perspective is not, ortho rays are parallel (and distinct
rays for distinct cursors) and the cursor closes through the matrix,
sizes ignore depth where perspective shrinks them, the mode switch agrees
at the target plane, the ortho dolly holds the cursor point, and the
camera transforms carry the mode. In the egui shell:
`projection_radios_flip_the_viewport_mode` (real pointer events, queues
nothing) and `bare_p_flips_projection_without_a_command` (P toggles,
Ctrl+P still arms the post dialog). Snapshots rebuilt for the new
browser row.

**Not exercised**

- No live GPU interaction test for the new pick path beyond the CPU
  matrix closure (`projection_tests`): the wgpu renderer just consumes the
  same `mvp` matrix, so the draw side rides existing `gpu_render` lanes.
- The sim's `PreviewCamera` (and trace.wgsl) deliberately stay
  perspective; ortho preview eyes are out of scope for #434.
- Gate (Windows): the whole quick tier went green end to end at this
  head on the first run after a boot - ui lib (338 unit tests) and
  every ui integration suite, `trace_parity` 5/5 and `trace_composite`
  4/4 included, under the lane's usual `--test-threads=6`; clippy
  `-D warnings` green. On repeat runs minutes later those two
  wgpu-heavy trace suites intermittently crash their process
  (STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION, a different test each time) while
  everything else stays green every run - it reproduces identically on
  plain **main**, and both go green back-to-back serially, so it rides
  no code here.

Changelog: feat(viewport): parallel (orthographic) projection - the browser's Projection radios and bare P flip it; zoom, pan, orbit, frame and picks keep working (#434)

Fixes #434

- `README.md` License section:
  - the license is Apache-2.0;
  - the contributors hold the copyright;
  - pull requests are licensed under Apache-2.0 (§5, inbound = outbound, no CLA);
  - MIT-era code is redistributed under Apache-2.0, which MIT permits.
- Packaging:
  - `aur/PKGBUILD` and `aur/.SRCINFO` say `Apache-2.0`, and the package installs `NOTICE`;

- `docs/decisions/452-license-apache.md`: the decision, the MIT terms the existing code was contributed under, and the options dropped (dual MIT/Apache, a CLA).

## How tested
- `git grep` finds no MIT reference left for CamCraft's own code. The README mentions MIT only in its history note, and the third-party notices are unchanged.
- No code changed, so there are no test suites to run.

## Not exercised
- No packaging run: AUR, deb/rpm, FreeBSD, macOS and the release workflow are only edited. The next release build exercises them.
